title: Microsurgical technique for tracheostomy in the rat
author: Ghali

steps.title: Prepare and anesthetize rat
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia in a spontaneously‑breathing adult male Sprague‑Dawley rat (340–380 g) with isoflurane (Matrix; 4–5 % induction, 1.85–2.15 % maintenance) vaporized in O₂ via a snout mask; place three subcutaneous electrodes and connect to a Neurolog (Digitimer, Hertfordshire, UK) amplifier with conventional filtering, then monitor the ECG with an audio amplifier (model AM10; Grass Instruments) and an oscilloscope, adjusting depth until withdrawal reflexes and heart‑rate responses to distal hind‑limb pinches are absent.

steps.title: Make ventral cervical incision
steps.instruction: Perform a ventral midline cervical incision from the manubrium sterni to the level of the hyoid bone.

steps.title: Expose trachea
steps.instruction: Bluntly dissect cervical soft tissue to expose the sternocleidomastoid and sternohyoid muscles; split the fascia overlying the paired sternohyoids in the midline and retract each sternohyoid laterally to reveal the trachea.

steps.title: Mobilize neurovascular bundle
steps.instruction: Identify and gently mobilize the inferior thyroid artery and recurrent laryngeal nerve away from the trachea, then place a suture underneath the trachea while avoiding this paratracheal neurovascular bundle.

steps.title: Incise trachea with electrocautery
steps.instruction: Using electrocautery, make a midline incision of the trachea caudal to the thyroid gland, extending approximately two cartilaginous tracheal rings to prevent inadvertent thermal damage.

steps.title: Insert and secure tracheal cannula
steps.instruction: Insert a tracheal cannula into the tracheal opening and secure it with a 3‑0 silk suture; create a “knot anchor” and use it to further lock the cannula to the trachea.

steps.title: Close cervical incision
steps.instruction: Close the cervical skin incision tightly using a continuous 4‑0 silk suture.

steps.title: Optional curved cannula
steps.instruction: If a cervical vertebral corpectomy is planned, substitute the standard cannula with a ventrally‑curved tracheal cannula.
